Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming to iOS 27, the Passwords app is getting a particularly powerful one: it can automatically change your passwords for you.

The Passwords app in iOS 27, powered by Apple Intelligence, can automatically fix compromised login credentials once you give it the green light.

The new generation of Apple Intelligence is at the heart of the upcoming iOS 27 and other accompanying software updates. One of the powerful new AI features relates to the Apple Passwords app.

The Passwords app launched two years ago as a dedicated hub for managing login credentials, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

If something's off with your password database, the app has long given you a heads-up. For instance, if your password has shown up in a data breach, or if you're reusing the same one across multiple accounts, the Passwords app will let you know.

Up until now, however, you've had to fix those compromised credentials yourself.

Apple says the new agentic AI capabilities in iOS 27 can change your passwords for you in many situations. According to its website:

With this feature, you can keep your login credentials secure and use strong passwords at all times, without having to lift a finger or spend time doing it yourself.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and will roll out to all users in the coming weeks. The new Passwords feature is expected to debut with iOS 27.0, but beta availability has been spotty, so it may not arrive until iOS 27.1.

Have you used the new Passwords feature in the iOS 27 beta? How was your experience? Let us know in the comments.
